author: MaxGhenis
body:
Investigated on policyengine-us 1.756.10 (git main @ a2cececb, 2026-07-05) (recomputed via the harness: policyengine + local taxsimtest binary). **This is a TAXSIM-35 bug: it has not implemented Wisconsin's new (TY2025) retirement income exclusion.**

Both engines agree on WI taxable income (**102,525**) and on the regular tax computed *without* the exclusion (PE `wi_income_tax_before_refundable_credits` = **4644.05**, TAXSIM `siitax` = **4651.88** — a rounding-level match). The gap is entirely the **Schedule SB Line 16 retirement income exclusion** under **Wis. Stat. § 71.05(6)(b)54m** (2023 Wis. Act 19), effective for tax years beginning after 2024:

- Up to **$24,000 per individual age 67+** ($48,000 joint if both qualify), **no federal-AGI limit and no income phase-out** (confirmed from the statute text of § 71.05(6)(b)54m.a and subd. b–e).
- Here the primary is 70 (eligible) and the spouse is 66 (not yet 67), so PE applies a **$24,000** exclusion on the primary's pension. Because claiming Line 16 forfeits credits, PE computes tax both ways and takes the lower: **3120.48** vs the no-exclusion **4644**.

TAXSIM applies **$0** exclusion (its result equals the no-exclusion path), so it appears not to have § 71.05(6)(b)54m for 2025. PE is statute-correct. Leaving open for the NBER report (grouped with #932, which is the same missing provision with both spouses 67+ -> $48,000 cap).
